Note on file, not evaluated by the rules: No new Liquor Stores. A Restaurant operating as a Bona Fide Eating Place may serve alcohol (licenses may be transferred in from inside or outside the SUD), as may non-profit theaters, bowling alleys/mini-golf with an integrated Restaurant, single-screen movie theaters (beer and wine) and ABC Type 90 music venues. A new or relocated Bar is considered under the underlying zoning but only as a Conditional Use, and must use a liquor license transferred from another Bar within the SUD. Existing liquor establishments may relocate or expand only with CU. East of the western boundary of the Mission Street NCT and north of Cesar Chavez Street, any new Restaurant requires CU and new ABC Type 75 (brewpub) licenses are prohibited. Good-neighbor operating conditions (§ 202.2 plus lighting and window-signage limits) apply.

approvals.approval: Place of Entertainment, Limited Live Performance or Fixed Place Outdoor Amplified Sound permit

basis.text: A live performance, a DJ or karaoke needs a Place of Entertainment or Limited Live Performance permit (one performer without amplification who ends by 10 p.m. needs none). Regular amplified sound outdoors needs a Fixed Place Outdoor Amplified Sound permit. The Entertainment Commission holds a public hearing on each application. Recorded music indoors with no performer needs no entertainment permit, and dancing by patrons needs no permit of its own. Where a permit is needed: further review.
basis.code_section: San Francisco Police Code § 1060 et seq. (Place of Entertainment; Limited Live Performance; Fixed Place Outdoor Amplified Sound)

referral_steps.text: Place of Entertainment Permit application: this application is sent to the Police Department for review (Police Code § 1060.2(b)(1); § 1060.5(a)).

A new or relocated Bar is considered under the underlying zoning but only as a Conditional Use, and must use a liquor license transferred from another Bar within the SUD. Existing liquor establishments may relocate or expand only with CU. East of the western boundary of the Mission Street NCT and north of Cesar Chavez Street, any new Restaurant requires CU and new ABC Type 75 (brewpub) licenses are prohibited. Good-neighbor operating conditions (§ 202.2 plus lighting and window-signage limits) apply.

filing_playbook.action: Register the business with the San Francisco Treasurer & Tax Collector to obtain a Business Account Number (BAN), and file a Fictitious Business Name statement with the County Clerk if the public-facing name differs from the legal entity name.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Register within 30 days of starting business in San Francisco. The fee is tiered by gross receipts (e.g. $55 up to $100k, $95 up to $250k for 2026–27, each plus a $4 state fee). The BAN is required for every other city permit. If operating under a DBA, file the FBN statement with the County Clerk, publish it once a week for four weeks in a court-approved newspaper, and file proof of publication within 45 days. Banks and ABC ask for the filed FBN statement.

filing_playbook.what_to_say: Email the Planning Department Zoning Information Counter (pic@sfgov.org) and ask: 'Does Planning Code § 249.60(b)(2)(C) permit upgrading the existing Type 41 license at 995 Valencia St to a Type 42 in place for a new bar use, or must a Type 42 be transferred from another bar premises within the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD?' If a transfer is required, engage an ABC license broker to identify Type 42 or Type 48 licenses at bars within the SUD that are available for purchase and transfer. Do not file the CUA or ABC application until this is settled in writing.

timeline_cost.notes: This timeline and cost range is for the approvals in the entitlement path when they are granted: Conditional Use Authorization (120–300 days, $3,100–$15,000), Place of Entertainment permit (45–120 days, $2,708–$3,800), health permit to operate (14–45 days, $470–$1,000), and building permit with change of use (14–120 days, $800–$15,000). The timeline assumes the CUA is filed after the SUD license-transfer question is settled in writing, the ABC Type 42 application or transfer is filed after the CUA is approved and the 30-day appeal period has run, the POE permit is filed in parallel with or after the ABC application, and the building permit and health permit are filed after the CUA and POE approvals are in hand. The 255–635 day range is measured from filing the CUA to obtaining the health permit and building permit final sign-off, assuming all approvals are granted. It does not include the time to identify and escrow a Type 42 license from another bar in the SUD (if a transfer is required), which can add 2–6 months before the CUA is filed. The cost range includes only city and Entertainment Commission fees, not the ABC license fee ($1,000–$1,600), the cost of purchasing a Type 42 license on the open market (if required, typically $5,000–$50,000+ depending on availability), or the cost of construction, architectural plans, or brokers. State and federal registrations (entity formation $70–$150, seller's permit $0, EIN $0, food safety certifications ~$100–$250, RBS training ~$3–$30 per person, workers' comp insurance premiums) and music licenses ($600–$5,000 per year for ASCAP and BMI) are not included. The timeline assumes no appeals, no Discretionary Review, no protests at the ABC or Entertainment Commission hearings, and no failed inspections. If the concept is formula retail (chain with 11+ locations), add the formula-retail review to the CUA hearing. If the floor area is 3,001 sq ft or more, the use-size trigger is already part of the CUA. The Building Code change-of-occupancy question is not settled, so the building permit timeline may be longer if a change of occupancy is required.
